newsitem.title: UK: BICC says some businesses face difficulties.
newsitem.headline: BICC says some businesses face difficulties.

text.p: British cable to construction group BICC Plc warned on Wednesday that some of its businesses still faced difficult conditions and that it planned to further reduce its exposure to German and Italian power cables.
The warning came in the group's interim report which added that the outlook for construction unit Balfour Beatty had improved and basic cable problems were being tackled.
Pre-tax profits were back in the black at 55 million pounds ($86.8 million) versus a two million pound, post-exceptional loss last year. The dividend was frozen at four pence per share.

Chairman Viscount Weir said in a statement, "Overall, therefore, although we still face difficult conditions in some parts of our business, the outlook for Balfour Beatty is better and we are making progress towards solving the basic problems in power cables."
On the power cable market in mainland Europe, BICC indicated it planned to cut staff levels further in German and Italian operations to reduce its exposure in those loss-making units.
Alan Jones, chief executive, added BICC planned to pare back its 700 jobs in Germany. That figure has already been reduced from over 2000.
"In Italy we have recently agreed a plan with the government and trade unions to reduce our numbers employed by a further 350 people," he said. That should have an impact by the second half.
The results themselves showed pre-tax profits down 13 percent compared to last year's underlying profit figure of 63 million pounds, before charges.
BICC said the improved performance from its construction unit had not been enough to balance continuing losses in power cables in Europe and a "duller performance in Australia."
Group sales fell to 2.22 billion pounds in the six month period to June 28, from 2.37 billion the previous year.
